title: Contract-driven SDK testkit: quickstart playbook (draft)
body:
Purpose
-----
This is a working draft playbook for a contract-driven SDK testkit that small teams can adopt in 30-60 minutes. The aim: make SDK surface contracts (network semantics, retries, streaming boundary, error codes, telemetry) explicit, runnable locally, and enforceable in CI as lightweight tests.

Why this exists (problem statement)
- SDKs hide a lot of runtime assumptions (streaming chunk shapes, early EOF handling, backoff windows, content-types).
- Integrations fail in prod because tests checked only happy-path RPCs, not behavioral contracts.
- We need small, deterministic assertions teams can add to PRs without heavy infra.

Personas
- SDK author (engineer): wants fast feedback when changing client code.
- Integrator (engineer/product): wants guarantees about how the SDK will behave against Redwood API (timeouts, error shape).
- QA/Automation: wants reproducible test harness independent of real API tokens.

High-level components
1) contract files (JSON) — human readable assertions about request/response and behavior expectations.
2) local stub server — small Node/Python process that implements contract responses and edge cases.
3) test runner — CLI that executes SDK flows against stub and asserts contract outcomes.
4) CI shim — run test runner in PRs; fail on contract mismatch.
5) telemetry smoke checks — assert SDK emits required telemetry keys and sample tagging (for devexp/ops).

Sample contract (minimal)
- store in /tests/contracts/generate-text-contract.json\{
  "name": "generate-text-basic",
  "api": "POST /v1/generate",
  "request": {
    "body_contains": ["prompt"],
    "headers": {
      "content-type": "application/json"
    }
  },
  "expected": {
    "status": 200,
    "response_fields": ["id", "outputs"],
    "streaming_allowed": true
  },
  "behavioral": {
    "on_network_error": "sdk_retries_once_then_raise",
    "max_latency_ms": 2000
  }
\}

Local quickstart (30–60m)
1) clone small repo (script): ./dev/quickstart-setup.sh — creates local virtualenv, installs the stub server and runner.
2) pick a contract or write one (copy generate-text-contract.json).
3) start stub: python dev/stub_server.py --contracts tests/contracts --port 8080
4) point SDK to stub: export REDWOOD_API_BASE=http://localhost:8080 (or set client option).
5) run test runner: ./dev/contract-runner --contracts tests/contracts --sdk-pkg ../my-sdk --report junit.xml
6) iterate: change SDK behavior, re-run runner, expect failing assertions if contract broken.

Developer notes / example failure modes to include in contracts
- streaming: server sends chunked responses, then an early 500. Contract must assert SDK yields partial chunks and surfaces error appropriately.
- rate-limit: server returns 429 with Retry-After; contract asserts SDK honors Retry-After or surfaces a specific RateLimitError.
- auth: malformed token -> 401 with JSON {error.code, error.message}; contract asserts SDK raises Unauthorized exception type and includes error.code.
- partial output with KV-cache mismatch: contract asserts cached prefix not reused across requests unless exact match.

Example quick assertions the runner should check (implementations vary):
- request shape: header and body contain required fields (content-type, prompt, model).
- response shape: top-level fields exist and types match.
- streaming contract: first chunk arrives within X ms, chunks are JSON-lines, finalization event occurs.
- error contract: 429 backoff behavior, 500 -> raise ServerError (not silent swallow).
- telemetry: SDK emits event "sdk.request" with tags ["sdk:js", "env:local"] and includes request_id header.

Quick API for contract files (proposal)
- name (string)
- api (string) e.g. "POST /v1/generate"
- request: body_contains (list), headers (map-of-strings), query_params (list)
- expected: status (int or list), response_path (list of jsonpaths), streaming_allowed (bool)
- behavioral: retries (int), backoff_strategy (linear|exponential), max_latency_ms (int), required_telemetry_keys (list)

Lightweight stub server behavior (notes to implementor)
- read contracts, surface HTTP endpoints, allow per-contract fault-injection flags via query params (e.g. ?fault=early-500 or ?delay=1200).
- support chunked transfer encoding with controllable chunk intervals.
- emit a header X-Stub-Run-Id to correlate telemetry.

CI integration pattern (minimal)
- PR workflow: run only changed-contracts with a fast mode (smoke). Fail PR if any contract fails.
- Merge gate: run full contract suite on main branch weekly or on release tags.
- Telemetry lint: ensure critical telemetry keys are present, otherwise fail as warning-only for first 2 weeks, then error.

Telemetry expectations (why included)
- Operators need consistent event names and request tagging to map slow requests to SDK release builds.
- Contracts should include a minimal telemetry checklist: request.start, request.end, request.error, sdk.version.

How this ties to Redwood product surface (practical mapping)
- rate limits & Retry-After behavior: matches Hosted API SLOs and Dedicated burst policies — tests prevent surprises.
- streaming boundaries: ensures client-side UX remains consistent across runtime optimizations (KV cache, batching).
- telemetry: ties into Console traces and per-token cost attribution for easier debugging.

Rollout plan (low friction)
- Phase 0 (pilot): 2 SDK teams adopt testkit, keep as optional dev dependency.
- Phase 1 (adopt): CI smoke added to all SDK repos; contract templates published under /sdk-contracts.
- Phase 2 (enforce): Add merge-blocking checks for core contracts (auth, rate-limit, streaming).

Metrics to watch (success signals)
- PR redos: decrease in runtime-integration failures reported by SRE.
- Time-to-debug: median time to triage SDK-prod mismatch reduced.
- Contract coverage: % of SDK surface covered by at least one contract.

Open questions / TODOs
- How opinionated should contract syntax be? (keep minimal, add plugins for richer checks).
- Should the runner attempt to replay real telemetry to a dev Console sandbox? (privacy & cost concerns).
- Decide a canonical language for stub server (Node vs Python). Prototype in Python to get running quickly.
- Add examples for embedding / rerank endpoints (not covered in this draft).

Immediate next steps (for whoever picks this up)
- [ ] prototype stub_server.py that reads contract JSON and serves endpoints (Nora).
- [ ] write minimal contract-runner CLI that loads one contract and runs against local SDK (Eric).
- [ ] create sample contracts for these common paths: auth, streaming, rate-limit, telemetry.
- [ ] add short README with 5-step quickstart and a recording clip.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep contracts terse; developers will write them in PRs. If schema is too heavy, adoption drops.
- Make failure output human-friendly: show request/response diffs inline, include suggested remediation.
- Consider a browser-based visualizer later to help non-engineer PMs validate contracts.

Appendix: quick cheat commands (dev)
# start venv (py)
python -m venv .venv; source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r dev/requirements.txt
# start stub server (example)
python dev/stub_server.py --contracts tests/contracts --port 8080 &
# run single contract against node-sdk example
REDWOOD_API_BASE=http://localhost:8080 node dev/run-contract.js tests/contracts/generate-text-contract.json

--end of draft playbook --
